boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named public-facing destinations on the Lake Washington Boulevard, Lake Street, Kirkland Avenue, Market Street, and Waverly Way corridors in Northwest University’s Kirkland orbit.

cards.title: Houghton Beach Park: pier and dock
cards.subtitle: Lake Washington Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Walk the Lake Washington Boulevard corridor to view the long pier and dock; check the City’s current beach-status notice before planning any swim.
cards.short_summary: A named waterfront park with a long pier and dock.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Houghton Beach Park at 5811 Lake Washington Boulevard and describes its long pier and large dock.
cards.access_notes: Review the City’s current swimming-beach notices before entering the water.

cards.title: 2nd Ave South Dock: waterfront stop
cards.subtitle: Lake Street South / Lake Washington Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Use this map-listed dock as a short waterfront stop south of Marina Park; remain on public dock areas and follow posted moorage rules.
cards.short_summary: A City-listed dock immediately south of Marina Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says 2nd Avenue South Dock, commonly called South Dock, is south of Marina Park at 203 Lake Street South.
cards.source_title: 2nd Ave South Dock — City of Kirkland
cards.access_notes: City-listed hours are sunrise to 10 PM; follow posted dock and moorage rules.

cards.title: Marina Park: public art and pavilion
cards.subtitle: Lakeshore Plaza / Lake Street corridor
cards.notes: Visit the park’s public-art pieces and open-air pavilion from the Lakeshore Plaza corridor; picnic tables are available first-come, first-served.
cards.short_summary: A downtown waterfront park with art, beach, pavilion, and boat facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Marina Park as a downtown Lake Washington park with a sandy beach, public art, open-air pavilion, boat launch, and dock.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are sunrise to 10 PM; the parking lot is paid.

cards.title: Peter Kirk Park: courts and public art
cards.subtitle: Kirkland Avenue / 3rd Street corridor
cards.notes: Head to the 3rd Street side for the skate park, basketball court, public art, and seasonal pool; use the year-round restroom on the west side.
cards.short_summary: A downtown park with recreation spaces, sculptures, and public Wi-Fi.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Peter Kirk Park’s skate park, basketball court, playground, seasonal pool, public art, year-round restroom, and public Wi-Fi.
cards.source_title: Peter Kirk Park — City of Kirkland
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are sunrise to 11 PM; pool access and programmed facilities may have separate rules.

cards.title: Kirkland Library: quiet room view
cards.subtitle: Kirkland Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use the library’s quiet room overlooking Peter Kirk Park for a reading break; confirm same-day hours and any room-use rules before you go.
cards.short_summary: A public library with a quiet room overlooking Peter Kirk Park.
cards.evidence_claim: KCLS lists Kirkland Library at 308 Kirkland Avenue and notes a quiet room overlooking Peter Kirk Park.
cards.source_title: Kirkland Library — King County Library System
cards.access_notes: KCLS publishes variable daily hours; check its location page before visiting.

cards.title: Kirkland Performance Center: performance calendar
cards.subtitle: Kirkland Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Check the official calendar for an all-ages-appropriate performance or arts event, then use the posted box-office and accessibility information to plan.
cards.short_summary: A Kirkland Avenue venue for live performances and arts programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Kirkland Performance Center’s official site lists live performances and its address at 350 Kirkland Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Ticketing, age guidance, and event times vary; use the official event listing before attending.

cards.title: Everest Park: fields and pickleball
cards.subtitle: 8th Street South corridor
cards.notes: Take the 8th Street South corridor to the park’s pickleball courts, trails, playground, and ball fields; use the City’s schedule for field availability.
cards.short_summary: A community park with drop-in pickleball, ball fields, and a trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Everest Park’s pickleball courts, four ball fields, playground, picnic shelter, restrooms, and trail.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are dawn to dusk; some field use may require a permit.

cards.title: Heritage Park: interpretive walk
cards.subtitle: Waverly Way corridor
cards.notes: Follow the interpretive walk through the park, then see Heritage Hall and its gardens from the Waverly Way side; courts are drop-in only.
cards.short_summary: A Market-neighborhood park with an interpretive walk and Heritage Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says Heritage Park has Heritage Hall and gardens, tennis courts, a play area, an interpretive walk, and a grass field.
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are sunrise to 11 PM; Heritage Hall rentals have separate terms.

cards.title: Waverly Beach Park: carved benches
cards.subtitle: Waverly Way corridor
cards.notes: Continue along Waverly Way to see the carved cedar bench series and waterfront dock; check current water-quality updates before any swimming plan.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront park with carved public art, dock, and beach facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Waverly Beach Park’s carved cedar bench series, dock, playground, picnic areas, and swimming beach.
cards.source_title: Waverly Beach Park — City of Kirkland
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are sunrise to 10 PM; swimming conditions and lifeguard availability can change.

cards.title: Kirkland Arts Center: gallery and classes
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor
cards.notes: Stop at the Market Street gallery during posted exhibition hours, or browse the official workshop listings for an age-appropriate class before registering.
cards.short_summary: A Market Street arts center with a gallery and visual-arts workshops.
cards.evidence_claim: Kirkland Arts Center lists its location at 620 Market Street and invites visitors to view its professional, non-commercial gallery or take visual-arts classes.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit — Kirkland Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Gallery and class hours vary; some specific workshops are restricted to adults, so review the individual listing.

warnings: Several destinations are in downtown Kirkland rather than immediately adjacent to campus; verify travel routing and current access conditions before leaving campus.
